## Description

The Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM) method is a predictor-corrector multistep scheme
for initial value problems $y' = f(t,y)$. In the 4-step form, an explicit
Adams-Bashforth predictor estimates $y_{n+1}$ from recent history, and an implicit
Adams-Moulton corrector immediately refines it.

Because ABM is not self-starting, initial points are generated with a one-step method
(such as RK4). After startup, each new value uses prior function evaluations, giving
high accuracy with low per-step cost.

## Animations

The animation below reconstructs legacy Example 11 from the Mathews module:
$y' = 1 - t\sqrt[3]{y}$, $y(0)=1$, over $0 \le t \le 5$, computed with $n=200$ steps
($h=0.025$) instead of the $n=50$ steps ($h=0.1$) of the module's first run (see Behavior).
Each frame adds four steps (0.1 in $t$); the connecting curve passes through every
computed point.

The dashed black curve is a high-accuracy reference trajectory computed with fixed-step
RK4 at $h=10^{-4}$, since no closed-form exact solution is used for this case.

### Case 1 - ABM4 predictor-corrector, $y' = 1 - t\sqrt[3]{y}$, $y(0)=1$, $0 \le t \le 5$, $n=200$ steps ($h=0.025$)

**Behavior:** With $h=0.025$ the ABM4 values stay within $3.1\times10^{-7}$ of the exact
solution at all 201 step points (the largest error is near $t=3.3$), and the error at
$t=5$ is $2.6\times10^{-11}$ (exact $y(5)=0.0081199$). For steps longer than about
$h=0.0311$, $h\,|\partial f/\partial y|$ exceeds the ABM4 predictor-corrector's stability
limit $1.285$ before $t=5$ (because $\partial f/\partial y=-t/(3y^{2/3})$ reaches $-41.3$ at
$t=5$), and from then on errors are amplified instead of damped; just above $h=0.0311$
this affects only the last steps, but at the module's $h=0.1$ ($n=50$) it starts at
$t\approx3.45$, and the computed values fall to $y_{48}\approx-0.0018$ at $t=4.8$ (below
zero), then turn upward and end at $y(5)\approx0.138$, about 17 times the exact value.

[Julia source](adamsbashforthmoultonaa.jl)
